sources.terrain: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA/Airbus; TanDEM-X/DLR data), AWS Open Data s3://copernicus-dem-30m
sources.polar_moon_terrain: LOLA RDR (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter, LRO/NASA; PDS), USGS Astrogeology COPC copy on AWS (s3://asc-moon/hobu), gridded by us at 60 m
sources.moon_terrain: SLDEM2015 (LOLA + Kaguya TC; Barker et al. 2016, Icarus 273:346), 512 px/degree, USGS copy on AWS (s3://asc-moon)
sources.earth_craters: Earth Impact Database (PASSC, Univ. New Brunswick)

crater_units.diameter_m: m (2 x radius of the circle fitted to rim points)
crater_units.depth_m: m (median rim elevation minus the 5th percentile of elevation within 0.9 R)
crater_units.rim_height_m: m (median across 72 directions of rim elevation minus surrounding terrain elevation at 1.5–2 R)
crater_units.wall_slope_p90: degrees (90th percentile within the same range)
crater_units.circularity: 4πA/P² of the rim outline (1 = perfect circle)
crater_units.rim_coherence: fraction of the 72 directions in which the rim is above the interior and surrounding terrain
crater_units.radial_profile_z_rel: mean radial profile: 0 = floor, 1 = rim; radial_profile_r_R axis = distance/radius

crater_warnings: Earth and Moon were measured using the same code on the same 60 m grid (aggregated 30 m Copernicus; LOLA gridded at 60 m; 59 m SLDEM2015).
The Brazilian craters are 65 to 255 million years old and heavily eroded: the bowl shape has disappeared, leaving the internal structure (central uplift, rings). The Moon has almost no erosion.

Targets with catalog diameters were measured using a guided search (0.8 to 1.2 x the catalog diameter). Blind search, without a prior hint, is used at non-crater sites (controls) and is reported as 'blind_search' for the others.
Internal structure (bowl, flat floor, central peak, terraces, ring) is classified using rules applied to the mean profile: it is an estimate.
Slope depends on resolution: at 60 m, walls appear less steep than in 5 m DEMs.

Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model (DSM): vegetation is included in the terrain. LOLA uses laser measurements, including within permanently shadowed areas; point density decreases with distance from the pole.
SLDEM2015 has stitching stripes in some locations (visible at Censorinus); they have little effect on the rim and floor but may bias slope estimates.

units.mean_height: m (mean crest prominence above the neighboring depression, in the original terrain)
units.probable_wind_direction: degrees from north, direction toward which the wind blows (0–360)
units.mean_spacing: m (between neighboring crests, perpendicular to them)
units.aridity_index: dimensionless, P/ET0 (UNEP: <0.05 hyper-arid; <0.2 arid; <0.5 semi-arid; <0.65 dry subhumid)

warnings: All metrics are automated estimates derived from a 30 m DEM; they do not replace imagery-based mapping and fieldwork.
Dunes with wavelengths shorter than ~120 m are not resolved; heights tend to be underestimated.
Copernicus GLO-30 is a digital surface model (DSM): vegetation and buildings are included in the terrain.
dune_type is classified using simple rules and should be treated as an estimate.
Detection thresholds were calibrated on the 12 sites in this version (4 with dunes, 8 without).
